P001.text: Treat each of the 14 sampled orders lacking a purchasing-system approval attachment as a transaction with a partially documented history.

P002.text: The supplied finding establishes an attachment gap, not that approval was absent.

P003.text: For each order, establish its identity, value, placement date, applicable threshold and approval requirements, and the authority of any purported approver.

P004.text: Do not assume all 14 required approval or that meeting minutes or delegated-authority forms necessarily satisfy the rule.

P005.text: Preserve the original review finding and gather each flagged order's purchasing record, dated approval records, relevant meeting minutes, delegated-authority forms and available audit history.

P006.text: Cross-check order identifiers, supplier, amount, scope, people and dates across these sources.

P007.text: Reconstruct the supported sequence from any delegation of authority through approval to order placement and later attachment or amendment.

P008.text: Distinguish the date approval reportedly occurred from the date its documentation was created or uploaded; a delegation establishes authority only within its terms and does not by itself establish approval of a particular order.

P009.text: Identify copied or derivative records rather than counting them as independent corroboration.

P010.text: Mark unsupported intervals and conflicting links explicitly.

P011.text: Request missing originals or clarification from relevant record custodians, recording searches, responses and remaining uncertainty.

P012.text: Set a reporting cutoff before the board review in three weeks.

P013.text: Close a case when applicability and the relevant sequence are adequately supported; otherwise stop active reconstruction at the cutoff, or when identified sources are exhausted or inaccessible, and report the case as unresolved with a named follow-up owner and next step.

P014.text: Link recovered records to their orders while retaining their actual dates and the original attachment-gap finding.

P015.text: Look for independently originating records that agree on the same order, an approver's authority at the relevant time, the scope of approval and its documented occurrence before placement.

P016.text: Observe separately whether an attachment was merely uploaded later, whether documentation was first created after placement, or whether approval itself occurred afterward.

P017.text: Conflicting dates, mismatched amounts or identities, unclear delegation terms, unsupported retrospective statements and missing links signal uncertainty.

P018.text: Record these as proposed checks and possible findings, not as observations already made.

P019.text: Compatible links can support a bounded account that a particular order had documented approval before placement despite its missing attachment, provided the evidence satisfies the internal rule.

P020.text: Supported timing showing approval only after placement can establish that the identified approval was late, while leaving open whether another earlier approval existed.

P021.text: A verified exemption can establish that approval was not required for that order.

P022.text: Unsuccessful searches warrant saying that qualifying prior approval was not located within the recorded search scope.

P023.text: Prepare the board account with case-level evidence, established transitions, contradictions and unresolved gaps.

P024.text: Pursue attachment or indexing changes where evidence supports a filing problem; pursue authority clarification where delegation is unclear; and propose a pre-order approval check where the reconstructed sequence supports a timing or control problem.

P025.text: Assign unresolved record requests and any proposed changes owners and dates.

P026.text: Records may be missing, inaccessible, inaccurate, altered, ambiguous or copied from a common source.

P027.text: A later account of an earlier approval does not automatically establish contemporaneous documentation, and an upload timestamp alone does not date the approval.

P028.text: A complete-looking chronology may join different orders or conceal undocumented transitions.

P029.text: Missing attachments or unsuccessful searches do not prove that approval never occurred.

P030.text: Conversely, an attachment alone does not establish valid, timely approval.

P031.text: Do not extrapolate the 14-of-90 attachment finding into an organization-wide approval-failure rate without evidence about sampling and the remaining records.

P032.text: The reporting cutoff limits the investigation, not the underlying uncertainty; later evidence should trigger a dated revision.

P033.text: Apply the internal rule without drawing legal conclusions.
